Possible late and long-term effects of c.Explanation: Fatigue is a common issue among cancer survivors. It is recommended to assess for fatigue and treat any causative factors such as anemia, thyroid dysfunction, and cardiac dysfunction. Additionally, treatment or referral should be offered for factors impacting fatigue, such as mood disorders, sleep disturbance, and pain. Counseling patients to engage in regular physical activity and referring them for cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is also advised.

Cognitive impairment in cancer survivors may be linked to factors such as fatigue, insomnia, depression, adjuvant chemotherapy, surgery/anesthesia, endocrine therapy, and cancer itself. Older adults or those with lower cognitive reserves may be more susceptible. Genetic factors associated with estrogen metabolism genes may also play a role. Treatment for cognitive impairment is not well established, but some pharmaceuticals like modafinil have shown success.

Cancer survivors may experience chronic pain as a late or long-term effect of cancer treatment. This pain can be influenced by factors such as the type and invasiveness of the tumor, the treatment regimen used, and the time since cancer treatment. Chemotherapy-Induced Peripheral Neuropathy (CIPN) is a specific pain syndrome recognized in cancer survivors.
